VeloU Strength

The weight-room engine behind VeloU's throwing programs - built so a new coach can run it, and an experienced one can reason about it.

Our job is not to build great weightlifters. It's to build great pitchers. Every program on this site is built around one job: balancing the stress demand of the weight room against the athlete's current throwing stress.

You're here to learn how VeloU trains a throwing athlete's strength - not just what to hand an athlete, but why each program exists, who it's for, and when to use it. Five principles make up the whole system: Movement Literacy and Tension Literacy, the Base every athlete builds first, then Force Control, Acceleration, and Applied Power - the three programs a force-plate diagnosis routes an athlete into once that base is there.

Use this site as a reference, not a one-time read: come back to it to explain a program to an athlete, decide whether to advance or hold someone in their current phase, or remind yourself what a split is actually protecting against.

How to Use This Site

Read top to bottom for the full picture, or jump straight to what you need - each section below does one job:

Concepts

The shared vocabulary and mechanics every program reuses - the ten movements, the five principles, how level is set, the phase engine, loading splits, and durations. Learn it once.
Programs

Every built program, phase by phase and split by split - the actual sets, reps, loads, and exercises a coach hands an athlete.
How to Adjust

The judgment layer: how to move an athlete between phases, splits, and durations as their capacity and throwing calendar change.

Concepts

Every program in this site is built from the same handful of ideas - how an athlete is categorized, how a phase sets intensity, how a split manages throwing load. Learn the concepts once here, and every program page below becomes a quick reference instead of something new to learn.

The Ten Basic Movements

"Our job is not to build a great weightlifter. It is to make them great pitchers. The weight room mirrors the mound."

Foundational - periodized
Squatperiodized every principle
Hingeperiodized every principle
Pullperiodized every principle
Pressperiodized every principle
Lungeperiodized every principle
Expressive - prep → applied power
Crawlprep + Movement Literacy
Sprintprep + Movement Literacy
Jumpprep + Movement Literacy
Carryprep + Movement Literacy
Rotateprep + Applied Power

This system splits Press and Pull into Horizontal/Vertical and adds Posterior chain for finer diagnosis - Movement Literacy alone uses the literal ten. Plane and mode (lateral, rotational, ballistic) dial into a pattern; they never add a new one.

The Five Principles

The first two are a fixed base every athlete runs in order. Force-plate testing then forks the athlete - per pattern - into whichever deficit is actually limiting them.

1Movement Literacybroad competency
→
2Tension Literacyisometric + eccentric
↓ force-plate diagnosis, per pattern
FCForce Controleccentric brake
ACAccelerationconcentric speed
APApplied Powerexpressed power

Diagnosis is per pattern: Force Control on squat while Acceleration on bench is normal, not an inconsistency. Every four-week tick can re-route a pattern into a different program.

Placing an Athlete's Level

There are several dependent and interdependent variables that go into categorizing an athlete into a specific rank at the start of their training, and specific ways an athlete transitions between these rankings. This level is interdependent between strength and throwing - an athlete can be highly proficient from the throwing perspective but very novice in the weight room, or vice versa.

Set at the initial evaluation - decides who builds the Base first, and paces how fast they move. Encoded by bracelet color so the room reads it instantly.

L1 Entry Movement Literacy → Tension Literacy first
L2 Developing Movement Literacy → Tension Literacy first
L3 Advanced Force base established - straight into a deficit
AgeTraining ageMaturationEnergy - PotentialEnergy - ProductionPlaying levelAthletic testing

Draft - input weighting and force-plate diagnosis thresholds are still being finalized. Treat Level as a coach's placement judgment today, not a computed score.

What Each Program Builds

An athlete is first categorized into either a Literacy program or an Advanced Focus program, based on several underlying factors. Literacy programs fit athletes with a lower biological/training age, or who don't yet have the prerequisite force production for the advanced programs. Advanced Focus programs each work to eliminate a specific deficit the athlete presents with during testing.

The main purpose of each program, in one line - what it exists to build in the athlete.

Movement Literacy
Build the body awareness vocabulary every other program requires.
Tension Literacy
Teach the athlete how to generate and utilize hydraulic amplification - a foundational component for producing elite force production.
Force Control
Develop eccentric force/power production.
Acceleration
Develop concentric force/power production.
Applied Power
Develop a unified force/power profile.

The Phase Engine - Intensity

The phase is the athlete's current position on this deficit's force→power arc. It sets the load band and how the rep is executed - nothing to do with throwing, that's the split's job (next section).

P1
Load band opens, constraint loosest
→
P2
Load climbs, the constraint sharpens
→
P3
Load peaks, the constraint is tightest, closest to power

See the live values for each phase - load band, hold, concentric method, and the 4-week wave - on the Programs pages; they're pulled straight from phases.yaml / waves.yaml so this page never has to repeat numbers that can drift.

Using the Phases - Linear or Not

Linear
P1→P2→P3

A full build, bottom to top.

Non-linear
Diagnosis→any phase⟲ hold / advance / regress

Enter where the diagnosis warrants; move at each re-diagnosis point.

An advanced athlete may live in P2–P3 indefinitely. A returning or beat-up athlete drops back to P1, even if they trained at P3 before - the phase is a statement about CURRENT capacity, not a ladder everyone climbs from the bottom.

Loading Splits - Throwing Demand

The other axis, independent of the phase - it shapes the week around the athlete's CURRENT throwing load, not their lifting capacity. As throwing demand rises, volume comes down and vehicles shift from axial (free-bar) to non-axial (machine/de-loaded spine) to keep stress off the exact structures throwing is already taxing.

Rule of thumb: pick the split for the throwing period right now. Pick the phase for the athlete's capacity right now. The two choices don't influence each other.

Restructure 6d
Axial

Throwing load is near zero - full axial loading, every pattern gets a heavy + a light touch. Nothing is compromised for throwing yet.

→
Energy 5d
Axial

Throwing is building back up - lifting consolidates onto the throw-anchor days; lower-body volume steps back on those days. Still axial vehicles.

→
Wattage / Integrate 5d
Non-Axial

Throwing intensity is high - lower-body vehicles de-axialize (leg press, glute, Jefferson) to pull spinal load off the athlete exactly when arm/mound stress peaks.

→
Refine / Engage 4d
Non-Axial

Competition is close - 3 lift days each condense a primary, a reduced 2nd primary, and a 3rd pattern run as accessory, plus a speed-focused Friday Primer and two full recovery days.

Throwing demand, left to right - a coach follows this order as the throwing period advances through a season, and reverses it as demand drops back off.

Durations - Runway, Not Load

Every phase × split comes in three lengths. Exercises and day layout are identical across all three - only the weekly wave changes. A longer duration buys ACCUMULATION, never a higher load.

2-week
Peak fortnight - no separate deload
4-week
Build → build → peak → deload
8-week
Two 4-week ticks - 2nd adds volume, not load

A Deeper Look Into The Programs

Base principles (level-gated, run in order) and deficit programs (force-plate diagnosed, per pattern). A coach selects one deficit program per athlete-pattern - programs do not run in sequence.

Base Principles

Level-gated prerequisites - run in order before force-plate diagnosis routes an athlete into a deficit program.

Movement Literacy

LIVE

Body control and movement vocabulary, across all ten basic movements.

Gain control of the body. Build a broad vocabulary of competency across all ten basic movements and develop positional awareness through long-duration isometrics and tempo work - before any pattern gets a real load.

P14 wk
Flood the Variety
All ten patterns, every session - a 6-day rotation, Lower (Squat/Lunge/Hinge) alternating Upper (Press+Pull), volume rising gradually.
Bodyweight / light implement — Prep isometrics, then DB/KB-loaded foundational singles/pairs
P24 wk
Narrow & Deepen
The switch: foundational-focus days (long iso hold + real load) alternate with higher-volume expressive days - first true strength stimulus.
60–70% (RPE-anchored — this population isn't force-plate/1RM tested yet)
P34 wk
Introduce Tempo
Narrows to two tempo-eccentric lifts a day plus accessories - no prep, no expressive work. Primes exactly what Tension Literacy opens with.
65–75% (RPE-anchored)

P1 · Flood the Variety (Bodyweight / light implement — Prep isometrics, then DB/KB-loaded foundational singles/pairs)

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances. This phase also offers a 12-week wave for extra runway.

Who this phase fits

  • Every athlete entering the Base sequence - the entry point for a Level 1/2 athlete.
  • No training-age assumption - a movement-competency program, not a strength stimulus.
  • Every session: Prep superset → 2 expressive supersets → the day's foundational work.
  • LOWER day (Squat/Lunge/Hinge, 3 singles) alternates with UPPER day (2 Press/Pull pairs) across a 6-day cycle.

Watch for

  • Move to P2 once the athlete moves competently and confidently through every pattern at peak volume - real positions, not just finishing the session.
  • Every 4th week is a real Testing week, not a throwaway light week - its numbers decide readiness to advance.

Testing Day - Criteria to Advance

Every one of these must improve on the final Testing day to progress to the next phase.

Athleticism

  • Broad Jump
  • 5-10-5
  • 10 Yard Sprint

Strength

  • Bar Hang :30
  • Bottom of Push-up :30
  • Modified Handstand Push-up :30
  • Iso Inverted Row :30

The 6-Day Rotation

Same 3 (Lower) or 4 (Upper) patterns every day of a given type - a different named exercise, and a different rank, each time. Read a Lower day's chips top → bottom as most → least challenging that week.

D1 Lower
Squat Most challenging
Lunge 2nd most challenging
Hinge Least challenging
D2 Upper
Press [Horizontal]
Pull [Vertical]
Press [Vertical]
Pull [Horizontal]
D3 Lower
Lunge Most challenging
Hinge 2nd most challenging
Squat Least challenging
D4 Upper
Pull [Horizontal]
Press [Vertical]
Pull [Vertical]
Press [Horizontal]
D5 Lower
Hinge Most challenging
Squat 2nd most challenging
Lunge Least challenging
D6 Upper
Press [Vertical]
Pull [Horizontal]
Press [Horizontal]
Pull [Vertical]
ML•Axial•P1•6D - Movement Literacy (ML Split 1 · Circuit)

When to run this split

  • Movement Literacy P1, always - phase-locked, not throwing-demand-governed. A 6-day cycle, not a literal calendar week.

Watch for

  • LOWER (Squat/Lunge/Hinge + 2 expressive supersets, 7 exercises) alternates with UPPER (Press+Pull ×2 + 1 expressive superset, 6 exercises) - never all ten patterns on one day.
  • Don't thin the exercise pool to save prep time - each pattern draws a different named exercise every time it recurs.

What it does

A 6-day cycle, not a literal calendar week — space real rest days around it as the athlete's schedule needs (same convention as P3's ML3). LOWER (D1/D3/D5) and UPPER (D2/D4/D6) alternate; each is a 6-8 exercise circuit, never the ten-pattern flood of the old design.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

P2 · Narrow & Deepen (60–70% (RPE-anchored — this population isn't force-plate/1RM tested yet))

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances. This phase also offers a 12-week wave for extra runway.

Who this phase fits

  • An athlete with real competency across all ten patterns, ready for the first actual load and first long isometric holds.
  • Base strength gets built here - large volume, broad coverage, not depth on any one pattern yet.
  • Loads sit around 60-70% of capacity - 1RM isn't tested yet at this level, so intensity is RPE-anchored, not percentage-exact.

Watch for

  • Move to P3 once the athlete holds the full isometric duration without the position degrading.
  • ...and moves real (if moderate) load through full ROM on every pattern without technical breakdown.

Testing Day - Criteria to Advance

Every one of these must improve on the final Testing day to progress to the next phase.

Athleticism

  • Broad Jump
  • 5-10-5
  • Jump Height
  • 10 Yard Sprint
  • 30 Yard Sprint

Strength

  • Bar Hang :45
  • Bottom of Push-up :45
  • Modified Handstand Push-up :45
  • Iso Inverted Row :45
  • Iso Chin-up :15
ML•Axial•P2•6D - Movement Literacy (ML Split 2 · Switch)

When to run this split

  • Movement Literacy P2, always - a 6-day cycle, not a literal calendar week.
  • 3 foundational-focus days (D1/D3/D5, overcoming iso + pattern lift) alternate with 3 higher-volume expressive/FLOOD days - this alternation IS the phase's 'switch.'

Watch for

  • First phase where an under-supervised rep risks a technical breakdown, not just a wasted rep - coach the position, not just the count.
  • Each pattern lift progresses mid-block from a DB/KB variant to barbell - don't rush that switch ahead of the athlete owning the position.

What it does

The 'switch': a 6-day cycle, not a literal calendar week — space real rest days around it as the athlete's schedule needs (same convention as ML1/ML3). Three foundational-focus days (D1 Squat/Hinge, D3 Press/Pull, D5 Lunge/Posterior — an overcoming isometric superset with the pattern lift, which progresses mid-block to a barbell version) alternate with three higher-volume expressive/FLOOD days (D2/D4/D6 — Jump/Sprint/Crawl/Carry/Rotate, each day a different progressed pick).

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

P3 · Introduce Tempo (65–75% (RPE-anchored))

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances.

Who this phase fits

  • An athlete with real base strength and positional control (P2), ready for the first tempo-eccentric work.
  • Direct bridge into Tension Literacy - the exact skill TL's P1 opens with.
  • Loads sit around 65-75% of capacity, still RPE-anchored - the real addition this phase is tempo, the first time the eccentric gets a written count.

Watch for

  • Watch for a rushed eccentric - the written tempo count is real, not a suggestion.
  • No prep, no expressive work here - the whole session is the two tempo lifts and their accessories.

Testing Day - Criteria to Advance

Every one of these must improve on the final Testing day to progress to the next phase.

Athleticism

  • Broad Jump
  • 5-10-5
  • Jump Height
  • 10 Yard Sprint
  • 30 Yard Sprint
  • 60 Yard Sprint

Strength

  • Bar Hang :60
  • Push-up 25
  • Iso Handstand Hold :30
  • Iso Chin-up :30
  • Chin-up 5
ML•Axial•P3•6D - Movement Literacy (ML Split 3 · Narrow)

When to run this split

  • Movement Literacy P3, always - a 6-day cycle, not a literal calendar week. No prep.
  • Two tempo-eccentric lifts per day, then two accessory supersets - expressive work is gone by this phase.

Watch for

  • The narrowest phase in the sequence - watch the tempo count (3-0-3-0 climbing to 5-0-5-0) as closely as the load.

What it does

A 6-day cycle, not a literal calendar week — space real rest days around it. No prep. Two tempo-eccentric lifts per day (D1 Squat/Lunge, D2 Press(H)/Press(V), D3 Hinge/Pull(V), D4 Lunge/Posterior, D5 Press(V)/Press(H), D6 Pull(H)/Hinge), then two accessory supersets.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

Tension Literacy

LIVE

Generate tension through a movement via isometrics + eccentric control.

Learn to generate tension throughout a movement - overcoming and yielding isometrics paired with eccentric control - to elicit force in the foundational patterns. The last stop before force-plate diagnosis forks the athlete into a deficit program.

P14 wk
Overcoming + Sub-Max Eccentric
Overcoming isometric, then a sub-max eccentric-tempo lift of the same pattern. No supra-max load, no safe-reset requirement yet.
70–80%
P24 wk
Overcoming + Supra-Max Eccentric
Overcoming isometric, then a supra-max eccentric - load EXCEEDS 1RM, caught on a pendulum, pin, rack, or machine. Coach-guided only.
105–125%
P34 wk
Yielding + Concentric
Yielding isometric paired with a full concentric lift of the same pattern - the bridge straight into force-plate diagnosis.
75–85%

P1 · Overcoming + Sub-Max Eccentric (70–80%)

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances.

Who this phase fits

  • Default entry point for any athlete running the Base sequence - Level 1/2 land here after Movement Literacy.
  • No prior eccentric or isometric exposure assumed.

Watch for

  • Move to P2 once the athlete holds the overcoming isometric's max effort AND controls the full 3–5s eccentric tempo without the bar speeding up or the position breaking down.
TL•Axial•P1•6D - Tension Literacy (TL Split 1 · Circuit)

When to run this split

  • Tension Literacy P1, always - phase-locked, not throwing-demand-governed. A 6-day cycle, not a literal calendar week.

Watch for

  • The overcoming isometric always leads, before the eccentric-tempo lift of the same pattern - don't flip the order just because the iso feels like a warm-up.

What it does

A 6-day cycle, not a literal calendar week — space real rest days around it. Six pattern-pair days (D1 Squat/Lunge, D2 Press(H)/Press(V), D3 Hinge/Pull(V), D4 Lunge/Posterior, D5 Press(V)/Press(H), D6 Pull(H)/Hinge); each day pairs an overcoming isometric with an eccentric-tempo lift of the same pattern, then traditional accessory work.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

TL•Axial•P1•5D - Tension Literacy (TL1 Split · Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Tension Literacy P1, when 6 days a week isn't available - same exercises and numbers as TL1, just reassembled into a 5-day cycle (Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V); Fri Lunge/Posterior drops entirely).

Watch for

  • Nothing here is a new number - every cell is copy-pasted from TL1's own D1-D6. Only the day pairing changed.

What it does

A 5-day cycle -- Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V) -- reassembled from the same exercises and numbers as the Axial 6-day cycle (Wed and Fri reuse D2/D4 unchanged), just fewer days. Every day still pairs an overcoming isometric with a sub-max eccentric lift of the same pattern, then traditional accessory work.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

TL•Non-Axial•P1•5D - Tension Literacy (TL1 Split · Non-Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Tension Literacy P1, same 5-day pairing as TL1_AX5 but every lift swapped for a non-axial vehicle, plus a Friday Primer instead of a sixth pattern-pair day.

Watch for

  • Friday's Primer is not a lift day - an overcoming-isometric hold superset into a light eccentric-tempo touch, not a session to add volume to.

What it does

Same Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat pattern-pairing as the Axial 5-day (Squat/Hinge, Pull(H)/Pull(V), Press(H)/Press(V), Press(V)/Pull(V)), every exercise swapped for a non-axial vehicle, plus a Friday Primer ahead of the weekend built from Tension Literacy's own toolkit (not a deficit's speed/power work). Two full recovery days (Thu, plus Friday's own low volume) instead of one.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

P2 · Overcoming + Supra-Max Eccentric (105–125%)

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances.

Who this phase fits

  • An athlete with real control of P1's sub-max eccentric tempo, ready for a load-exceeds-1RM eccentric stimulus.
  • Requires a coach/partner who can safely reset the load every rep - pendulum, pin, rack, or machine catch. Not a phase to run short-staffed.
  • Shows clean position control under P1's sub-max eccentric even as fatigue accumulates - that's the signal they're ready to have real weight added to the bar.

Watch for

  • The highest-risk phase in the whole Base sequence - supra-max eccentric loading is unforgiving of a missed spot.
  • If the supervision setup isn't right, stay in P1 rather than force the progression.
TL•Axial•P2•6D - Tension Literacy (TL Split 2 · Circuit)

When to run this split

  • Tension Literacy P2, always - same phase-locked, 6-day cycle as TL1.

Watch for

  • The overcoming isometric's SETS match its supra-max eccentric partner's set count every week (hold stays 5-7s) - not a fixed iso set count.
  • Coach-guided only, never solo.

What it does

Same 6-day pattern-pair cycle as TL1 (D1 Squat/Lunge, D2 Press(H)/Press(V), D3 Hinge/Pull(V), D4 Lunge/Posterior, D5 Press(V)/Press(H), D6 Pull(H)/Hinge); each day pairs an overcoming isometric (sets matched to its partner) with a supra-max eccentric lift of the same pattern, caught on a pendulum, pin, rack, or machine, then traditional-tempo accessory work.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

TL•Axial•P2•5D - Tension Literacy (TL2 Split · Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Tension Literacy P2, same 5-day reassembly as TL1_AX5 - Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V).

Watch for

  • Still coach-guided only - the supra-max eccentric work is unchanged, just on fewer days.

What it does

A 5-day cycle -- Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V) -- reassembled from the same exercises and numbers as the Axial 6-day cycle (Wed and Fri reuse D2/D4 unchanged), just fewer days. Every day still pairs an overcoming isometric with a supra-max eccentric lift of the same pattern, then traditional accessory work.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

TL•Non-Axial•P2•5D - Tension Literacy (TL2 Split · Non-Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Tension Literacy P2, same 5-day pairing as TL2_AX5, non-axial vehicles, plus a Friday Primer.

Watch for

  • The Friday Primer stays light and coach-guided-free - an overcoming-iso hold into a very light concentric touch, nowhere near the phase's real supra-max eccentric loading.

What it does

Same Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat pattern-pairing as the Axial 5-day (Squat/Hinge, Pull(H)/Pull(V), Press(H)/Press(V), Press(V)/Pull(V)), every exercise swapped for a non-axial vehicle, plus a Friday Primer ahead of the weekend built from Tension Literacy's own toolkit (not a deficit's speed/power work). Two full recovery days (Thu, plus Friday's own low volume) instead of one.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

P3 · Yielding + Concentric (75–85%)

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances.

Who this phase fits

  • An athlete who's built real eccentric control (P1) and tolerated supra-max loading (P2), ready to express that as a real concentric lift.
  • Direct bridge into force-plate diagnosis - can run on the NA3 split instead if the season peaks first.
  • Has shown they can both generate max effort into an immovable object (P1's overcoming iso) and safely tolerate a supra-max eccentric load (P2) - P3 now asks them to express that as real, unassisted concentric force.

Watch for

  • Watch for the yielding hold being treated as a rest between concentric sets - it's a real, high-tension exposure, not a breather. Full effort on both halves of the pair.
TL•Axial•P3•6D - Tension Literacy (TL Split 3 · Circuit)

When to run this split

  • Tension Literacy P3, always - same phase-locked, 6-day cycle as TL1/TL2.

Watch for

  • The yielding isometric's SETS match its concentric partner's set count, but the HOLD climbs 10s→30s across the block - not a flat hold length.

What it does

Same 6-day pattern-pair cycle as TL1/TL2 (D1 Squat/Lunge, D2 Press(H)/Press(V), D3 Hinge/Pull(V), D4 Lunge/Posterior, D5 Press(V)/Press(H), D6 Pull(H)/Hinge); each day pairs a yielding isometric (sets matched to its partner, holds climbing 10s to 30s) with a full concentric lift of the same pattern, then traditional-tempo accessory work.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

TL•Axial•P3•5D - Tension Literacy (TL3 Split · Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Tension Literacy P3, same 5-day reassembly as TL1_AX5/TL2_AX5 - Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V).

Watch for

  • The -2.5%/week secondary-pattern reduction still applies wherever it did on TL3 - nothing about the day reassembly changes that convention.

What it does

A 5-day cycle -- Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V) -- reassembled from the same exercises and numbers as the Axial 6-day cycle (Wed and Fri reuse D2/D4 unchanged), just fewer days. Every day still pairs a yielding isometric with a full concentric lift of the same pattern, then traditional accessory work.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

TL•Non-Axial•P3•5D - Tension Literacy (TL3 Split · Non-Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Tension Literacy P3, same 5-day pairing as TL3_AX5, non-axial vehicles, plus a Friday Primer built from the same yielding-isometric-plus-light-touch toolkit as NA3.

Watch for

  • Friday's Primer is not a lift day - a yielding-isometric hold superset into a light concentric touch.

What it does

Same Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat pattern-pairing as the Axial 5-day (Squat/Hinge, Pull(H)/Pull(V), Press(H)/Press(V), Press(V)/Pull(V)), every exercise swapped for a non-axial vehicle, plus a Friday Primer ahead of the weekend built from Tension Literacy's own toolkit (not a deficit's speed/power work). Two full recovery days (Thu, plus Friday's own low volume) instead of one.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

FRI - PRIMER

Not a full lift day -- mirrors a Complex across the day's two key patterns at a fraction of the volume: a yielding-isometric hold superset immediately into a light concentric touch. Every element is about intent, not accumulation.

Element / ExerciseMethod / Cue Prescription
P1Lower - Yielding Iso Primer - Yielding Iso Pendulum Squat (bottom-position hold)Hold the pattern's most tension-demanding position -- superset immediately into the light touch below 2 × 15 s

P3Upper - Yielding Iso Primer - Yielding Iso Bench Press (bottom-position hold)Hold the pattern's most tension-demanding position -- superset immediately into the light touch below 2 × 15 s
P4Upper - Light Concentric Touch - Seated Chest PressVery light, full-ROM touch -- keeps the pattern sharp without adding fatigue this close to the weekend 2 × 5 @ 60%

TL•Non-Axial•P3•4D - Tension Literacy (TL3 Split · Non-Axial 4D)

When to run this split

  • Tension Literacy P3, volume down significantly for a 4-day week - same Mon/Wed/Sat pattern shape as TL1_NA4/TL2_NA4.

Watch for

  • PullH's B1/B2 slot on Wed carries a computed -2.5%/week reduction, same as TL2_NA4 - no natural 'secondary' PullH exists elsewhere in P3's own data either.
  • Friday's Primer trades the light concentric touch for a fast one - same speed-focused intent as the other two 4-day Primers.

What it does

Volume down significantly: three lift days (Mon Squat/Lunge/Posterior, Wed Hinge/Pull(H)/Press(V) at the heaviest load, Sat Press(H)/Pull(V)/Hinge at higher volume), each a primary + a secondary pattern + a 3rd pattern run as that day's accessory superset pair (two total supersets), plus a speed-focused Friday Primer ahead of the weekend. Two full recovery days (Tue, Thu) instead of one.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

Deficit Programs

Force Control

LIVE

Eccentric force → eccentric power. Braked and controlled - the concentric is walled off.

Develop eccentric braking power before chasing concentric output - without it, the body caps its own speed because it can't trust the stop. Every rep is a rapid eccentric into an abrupt, held stop; across the three phases the yielding-iso hold shortens as the load climbs.

P14 wk
Eccentric Force
Rapid eccentric → long yielding stop (15–45s, climbs across the block). Sub-max load, unassisted concentric - stop & hold the position.
70–80%
P24 wk
Transition
Same shape as P1, heavier - the hold stretches to 25–55s and the concentric is partner-aided. A linear progression, every number advanced.
80–90%
P34 wk
Eccentric Power
Highest load, shortest hold - near-max doubles/singles released to pins, 2-person reset. Eccentric POWER, not just force.
88–94%

P1 · Eccentric Force (70–80%)

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances.

Who this phase fits

  • The default entry point - new to Force Control, returning from a break, coming off a beat-up stretch, or an unclear re-diagnosis.

Watch for

  • Move to P2 once the athlete owns the P1 concentric cleanly and the held stop is stable across the whole load band - not just on a good day.
FC•Axial•P1•6D - Force Control (FC Split 1 · Circuit)

When to run this split

  • Force Control P1, always - phase-locked, since P1's week shape (plyo/braked-eccentric/yielding-iso circuit) only exists on this split. A 6-day cycle, not a literal calendar week.

Watch for

  • The depth-drop plyometric leads every day and skips deload weeks (W4, W8) entirely.
  • E1/E2 continue Tension Literacy P3's own numbers on that pattern - check the athlete actually finished P3 first.
  • G1/G2 is a second, self-contained accessory superset on its own P1-specific sets×reps table (no %1RM, no cluster notation).

What it does

A 6-day pattern-pair cycle (D1 Squat/Lunge, D2 Press(H)/Press(V), D3 Hinge/Pull(V), D4 Lunge/Posterior, D5 Press(V)/Press(H), D6 Pull(H)/Hinge). Each day: a depth-drop plyometric primer, the day's primary + secondary braked-eccentric lift (fixed 0:5:1:1 tempo), a yielding-iso hold, then two exercises continuing Tension Literacy P3's own accessory progression on that day's patterns.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

FC•Axial•P1•5D - Force Control (FC1 Split · Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Force Control P1, when 6 days a week isn't available - same exercises and numbers as FC1, reassembled into a 5-day cycle (Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V); Fri Lunge/Posterior drops entirely).

Watch for

  • Nothing here is a new number - every cell is copy-pasted from FC1's own D1-D6. Only the day pairing changed.

What it does

A 5-day cycle -- Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V) -- reassembled from the same exercises and numbers as FC1's Axial 6-day cycle (Wed and Fri reuse D2/D4 unchanged), just fewer days.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

FC•Non-Axial•P1•5D - Force Control (FC1 Split · Non-Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Force Control P1, same 5-day pairing as FC1_AX5 but every lift swapped for a non-axial vehicle, plus a Friday Primer instead of a sixth pattern-pair day.

Watch for

  • Friday's Primer is not a lift day - a low-height plyometric touch into a light braked-eccentric touch, not a session to add volume to.

What it does

Same Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat pattern-pairing as the Axial 5-day, every exercise swapped for a non-axial vehicle, plus a Friday Primer built from Force Control's own toolkit (plyometric touch into a light braked-eccentric touch). Two full recovery days (Thu, plus Friday's own low volume) instead of one.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

FRI - PRIMER

Not a full lift day -- mirrors a Complex across the day's two key patterns at a fraction of the volume: a low-height plyometric touch superset immediately into a light braked-eccentric touch. Every element is about intent, not accumulation.

Element / ExerciseMethod / Cue Prescription
P1Lower - Plyometric Touch - Depth Drop to PauseLow height, light intent -- superset immediately into the light touch below 2 × 1 @ light height
P2Lower - Light Braked-Eccentric Touch - Pause Pendulum SquatWell under the phase's real B/C loading -- keeps the pattern sharp without adding fatigue this close to the weekend 2 × 4 @ 55% (0:5:1:1)
P3Upper - Plyometric Touch - Push-up Depth Drop to PauseLow height, light intent -- superset immediately into the light touch below 2 × 1 @ light height
P4Upper - Light Braked-Eccentric Touch - Pause Machine Chest PressWell under the phase's real B/C loading -- keeps the pattern sharp without adding fatigue this close to the weekend 2 × 4 @ 55% (0:5:1:1)

P2 · Transition (80–90%)

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances.

Who this phase fits

  • An athlete who's controlled P1's ceiling and needs a sharper, heavier eccentric stimulus.
  • Also the right re-entry point for an advanced athlete easing back in, rather than starting all the way back at P1.

Watch for

  • P2 hands part of the concentric to a partner/coach - only works if the athlete trusts and uses the assist rather than fighting it.
FC•Axial•P2•6D - Force Control (FC Split 2 · Circuit)

When to run this split

  • Force Control P2, always - same phase-locked, 6-day cycle as FC1. A linear progression of FC1: same exercises, every number advanced.

Watch for

  • Same structure as FC1 - plyometric leads, C follows B at −5% load.
  • E1/E2 continue FC1's numbers; G1/G2 runs its own P2-specific table. Only the numbers differ.

What it does

A linear progression of FC1 — same 6-day pattern-pair cycle, same exercises, every number advanced. Each day: a depth-drop plyometric primer (higher/further), the day's primary + secondary braked-eccentric lift (same 0:5:1:1 tempo, higher band), a longer yielding-iso hold, then two exercises continuing FC1's own accessory progression on that day's patterns.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

FC•Axial•P2•5D - Force Control (FC2 Split · Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Force Control P2, same 5-day reassembly as FC1_AX5 - Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V).

Watch for

  • Still a linear progression of FC1's own reassembly - same exercises, every number advanced, same as FC1/FC2's own relationship.

What it does

A 5-day cycle -- Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V) -- reassembled from the same exercises and numbers as FC2's Axial 6-day cycle (Wed and Fri reuse D2/D4 unchanged), just fewer days.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

FC•Non-Axial•P2•5D - Force Control (FC2 Split · Non-Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Force Control P2, same 5-day pairing as FC2_AX5, non-axial vehicles, plus a Friday Primer.

Watch for

  • The Friday Primer stays light - a plyometric touch into a light braked-eccentric touch, nowhere near this phase's real partner-aided loading.

What it does

Same Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat pattern-pairing as the Axial 5-day, every exercise swapped for a non-axial vehicle, plus a Friday Primer built from Force Control's own toolkit (plyometric touch into a light braked-eccentric touch). Two full recovery days (Thu, plus Friday's own low volume) instead of one.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

P3 · Eccentric Power (88–94%)

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances.

Who this phase fits

  • Advanced athletes at or near the top of current capacity - the goal is eccentric POWER, not just force.
  • Releases the bar to pins - assumes a coach/setup that can manage that safely.

Watch for

  • Highest load band, shortest held stop - the first phase shed when throwing demand spikes.
  • Don't be surprised to see an athlete pulled back to P2 mid-season for exactly that reason, not because anything went wrong.
FC•Axial•P3•6D - Force Control (FC Split 3 · Circuit)

When to run this split

  • Force Control P3, always - same phase-locked, 6-day cycle and exercise selection as FC2, carried over unchanged.

Watch for

  • B/C are NOT a continued tempo progression - restored to P3's own near-max scheme (doubles/singles, a (2x2) cluster on peak weeks, release to pins with a 2-person reset).
  • A/D/E1/E2 continue forward from FC2; G1/G2 runs its own P3-specific table, not a continuation of FC2's numbers.

What it does

Same 6-day pattern-pair cycle and exercise selection as FC2, carried over unchanged — but B/C's set/rep scheme and method are restored to Force Control P3's own original concept (near-max doubles/singles, a (2x2) cluster on peak weeks, release to pins with a 2-person reset) rather than continuing FC2's tempo-controlled lift. The accessory slots (A, D, E1/E2, G/H) continue forward from where FC2 finished.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

FC•Axial•P3•5D - Force Control (FC3 Split · Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Force Control P3, same 5-day reassembly as FC1_AX5/FC2_AX5 - Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V).

Watch for

  • B/C still restored to P3's own near-max release-to-pins scheme - nothing about the day reassembly changes that.

What it does

A 5-day cycle -- Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V) -- reassembled from the same exercises and numbers as FC3's Axial 6-day cycle (Wed and Fri reuse D2/D4 unchanged), just fewer days.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

FC•Non-Axial•P3•5D - Force Control (FC3 Split · Non-Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Force Control P3, same 5-day pairing as FC3_AX5, non-axial vehicles, plus a Friday Primer.

Watch for

  • Friday's Primer skips the real release-to-pins mechanism entirely - a plyometric touch into a light traditional-tempo touch, no pins, no 2-person reset.

What it does

Same Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat pattern-pairing as the Axial 5-day, every exercise swapped for a non-axial vehicle, plus a Friday Primer built from Force Control's own toolkit (plyometric touch into a light braked-eccentric touch). Two full recovery days (Thu, plus Friday's own low volume) instead of one.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

FRI - PRIMER

Not a full lift day -- the real release-to-pins work stays inside the real training days; this is a low-height plyometric touch into a light traditional-tempo touch, no pins, no 2-person reset. Every element is about readiness, not accumulation.

Element / ExerciseMethod / Cue Prescription
P1Lower - Plyometric Touch - Cat JumpLow height, light intent -- superset immediately into the light touch below 2 × 1 @ light height
P2Lower - Light Concentric Touch - Pendulum SquatVery light traditional tempo -- nowhere near this phase's real release-to-pins loading 2 × 5 @ 55%
P3Upper - Plyometric Touch - Push-up Depth Drop to PauseLow height, light intent -- superset immediately into the light touch below 2 × 1 @ light height
P4Upper - Light Concentric Touch - Machine Chest PressVery light traditional tempo -- nowhere near this phase's real release-to-pins loading 2 × 5 @ 55%

Acceleration

LIVE

Concentric force → concentric power. Dead-stop starts, VBT on the concentric throughout.

Move from no-momentum concentric output to momentum-aided output. The yielding iso is gone and eccentric load drops - every rep starts from a dead stop, pins or the rack do the stopping, and VBT tracks the concentric the whole way through.

P14 wk
Dead-Start Concentric
Every rep starts from zero, off the pins - little-to-no eccentric, pure concentric speed. Start progresses deep → shallow as load climbs.
67.5–82.5%
P24 wk
Rapid Descent to a Pause
Rapid eccentric descent → brief pause → maximal-intent concentric. A and B run full, identical volume; C is a slight-reduction third exposure.
77.5–92.5%
P34 wk
Reactive, No Pause
Rapid eccentric → no pause → reactive concentric. The fully explosive expression - stretch-shortening cycle doing real work.
85–95%

P1 · Dead-Start Concentric (67.5–82.5%)

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances.

Who this phase fits

  • Entry point for an athlete who's already demonstrated eccentric control (typically graduating Force Control), ready to chase bar speed.
  • Also right for re-entry after a layoff - start from a dead stop before adding eccentric back.

Watch for

  • Move to P2 once the athlete holds or improves bar speed as the start progresses deep → shallow - if speed drops as load rises, they're not ready for the eccentric yet.
AC•Axial•P1•6D - Acceleration (AC Split 1 · Circuit)

When to run this split

  • Acceleration P1, always - phase-locked, since P1's week shape (plyo/dead-start-concentric circuit) only exists on this split. A 6-day cycle.

Watch for

  • B/C have no fixed tempo code - VBT-metered, dead-start off the pins. Coach the bar speed, not a count.
  • D1/D2 is a literal copy of Force Control P1's own E1/E2 on the matching pattern - check that athlete's Force Control history first.
  • E1/E2 is a separate, plain sets×reps superset (no %1RM) on its own P1-specific table.

What it does

A 6-day pattern-pair cycle (D1 Squat/Lunge, D2 Press(H)/Press(V), D3 Hinge/Pull(V), D4 Lunge/Posterior, D5 Press(V)/Press(H), D6 Pull(H)/Hinge). Each day: a plyometric/reactive primer, the day's primary + secondary dead-start concentric lift off the pins (VBT-metered), then a superset pair (D1/D2) and a cluster pair (E/F) copied directly from Force Control P1's own accessory work on that day's patterns.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

AC•Axial•P1•5D - Acceleration (AC1 Split · Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Acceleration P1, when 6 days a week isn't available - same exercises and numbers as AC1, reassembled into a 5-day cycle (Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V); Fri Lunge/Posterior drops entirely).

Watch for

  • Nothing here is a new number - every cell is copy-pasted from AC1's own D1-D6. Only the day pairing changed.
  • Hinge's Monday slot carries a computed -5% reduction (this deficit's Hinge never has its own natural secondary appearance) - same convention as every other reduced pattern here, just derived instead of copied.

What it does

A 5-day cycle -- Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V) -- reassembled from the same exercises and numbers as AC1's Axial 6-day cycle (Tue/Wed/Fri reuse D6/D2/D4 unchanged), just fewer days.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

AC•Non-Axial•P1•5D - Acceleration (AC1 Split · Non-Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Acceleration P1, same 5-day pairing as AC1_AX5 - lower-body vehicles swapped non-axial (upper stays machine-based already), plus a Friday Primer instead of a sixth pattern-pair day.

Watch for

  • Friday's Primer is not a lift day - a light plyometric touch into a light dead-start touch, not a session to add volume to.

What it does

Same Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat pattern-pairing as the Axial 5-day, lower-body vehicles swapped non-axial (upper stays machine-based, already non-axial), plus a Friday Primer built from Acceleration's own toolkit (plyometric touch into a light dead-start/paused/reactive touch). Two full recovery days (Thu, plus Friday's own low volume) instead of one.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

AC•Non-Axial•P1•4D - Acceleration (AC1 Split · Non-Axial 4D)

When to run this split

  • Acceleration P1, volume down significantly for a 4-day week: Mon Squat/Lunge/Posterior, Wed Hinge/Pull(H)/Press(V) at the heaviest load, Sat Press(H)/Pull(V)/Hinge, plus a speed-focused Friday Primer.

Watch for

  • Each lift day's 3rd pattern supplies its own accessory pair, not its own primary lift - check the exercise names, not just the day header.
  • Pull(H)'s Wednesday slot carries a computed -5% reduction, same reason and same convention as Hinge's on AC1_AX5's Monday.

What it does

Volume down significantly: three lift days (Mon Squat/Lunge/Posterior, Wed Hinge/Pull(H)/Press(V) at the heaviest load, Sat Press(H)/Pull(V)/Hinge at higher volume), each a primary + a secondary pattern + a 3rd pattern run as that day's accessory pair (sourced from the 3rd pattern's own accessory vehicles, not the primary's), plus a speed-focused Friday Primer. Two full recovery days (Tue, Thu) instead of one.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

P2 · Rapid Descent to a Pause (77.5–92.5%)

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances.

Who this phase fits

  • An athlete who's fast off a dead stop, ready to re-introduce a real (if brief) eccentric without losing concentric intent.
  • The bridge between Force Control's world (an eccentric exists) and Acceleration's (the eccentric only loads the concentric).

Watch for

  • The paused stop is brief (1–2s) - if it turns into a mini yielding-iso hold, that's the wrong quality showing up. Cue speed out of the pause, not control through it.
AC•Axial•P2•6D - Acceleration (AC Split 2 · Circuit)

When to run this split

  • Acceleration P2, always - same phase-locked, 6-day cycle as AC1.

Watch for

  • The plyometric primer is gone - every day is three VBT-metered lifts.
  • A and B run the day's two patterns at FULL, identical volume - same %1RM, different bar speeds. C is a slight-reduction third exposure.
  • One accessory superset (D1/D2), plain sets×reps on its own P2-specific table (no %1RM).

What it does

Same 6-day pattern-pair cycle as AC1, restructured for P2: the day's two named patterns (A/B) run full, identical volume/reps/intensity (same %1RM, different bar-speed per exercise), plus a slight-reduction third exposure (C) of the primary pattern (~−5% load) — rapid eccentric descent to a brief paused stop, then maximal-intent concentric — then an accessory superset (D1/D2). No plyometric primer or cluster pair this phase.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

AC•Axial•P2•5D - Acceleration (AC2 Split · Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Acceleration P2, same 5-day reassembly as AC1_AX5 - Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V).

Watch for

  • P2's asymmetric shape carries over: Monday's Squat still gets a full exposure PLUS a slight-reduction third exposure (A+C); Hinge only gets the one full exposure (B), repositioned from its own home day, not reduced - this deficit's own convention, not a mistake.

What it does

A 5-day cycle -- Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V) -- reassembled from the same exercises and numbers as AC2's Axial 6-day cycle (Tue/Wed/Fri reuse D6/D2/D4 unchanged), just fewer days.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

AC•Non-Axial•P2•5D - Acceleration (AC2 Split · Non-Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Acceleration P2, same 5-day pairing as AC2_AX5, lower-body vehicles swapped non-axial, plus a Friday Primer.

Watch for

  • The Friday Primer stays light - a plyometric touch into a light paused-stop touch, well under this phase's real full-volume A/B loading.

What it does

Same Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat pattern-pairing as the Axial 5-day, lower-body vehicles swapped non-axial (upper stays machine-based, already non-axial), plus a Friday Primer built from Acceleration's own toolkit (plyometric touch into a light dead-start/paused/reactive touch). Two full recovery days (Thu, plus Friday's own low volume) instead of one.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

AC•Non-Axial•P2•4D - Acceleration (AC2 Split · Non-Axial 4D)

When to run this split

  • Acceleration P2, volume down significantly for a 4-day week - same Mon/Wed/Sat pattern shape as AC1_NA4.

Watch for

  • Wednesday's Pull(H) is repositioned from its own home day as a single full exposure (P2's own convention for its 'B'-role pattern), not a computed reduction like AC1/AC3's 4D.

What it does

Volume down significantly: three lift days (Mon Squat/Lunge/Posterior, Wed Hinge/Pull(H)/Press(V) at the heaviest load, Sat Press(H)/Pull(V)/Hinge at higher volume), each a primary + a secondary pattern + a 3rd pattern run as that day's accessory pair (sourced from the 3rd pattern's own accessory vehicles, not the primary's), plus a speed-focused Friday Primer. Two full recovery days (Tue, Thu) instead of one.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

P3 · Reactive, No Pause (85–95%)

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances.

Who this phase fits

  • Advanced athletes ready for the fully reactive expression - no pause, real stretch-shortening-cycle work.
  • The closest Acceleration gets to Applied Power's territory while staying a single-pattern lift.

Watch for

  • Highest load band, zero pause - the rep can collapse into a slow grind if intent drops.
  • First phase shed when throwing demand spikes - don't be surprised by a mid-season pullback to P2.
AC•Axial•P3•6D - Acceleration (AC Split 3 · Circuit)

When to run this split

  • Acceleration P3, always - same phase-locked, 6-day cycle as AC1/AC2.

Watch for

  • A is a 1½-rep primer at 80% of B's load, skipped on deload weeks.
  • B/C are reactive - no pause, unlike P2. Same rep scheme on both, C reduced ~5% off B.
  • D is a single VBT-metered accessory (not a superset) riding C's load - a few of its bar-speed targets are estimated off the closest pattern-family curve, not real vbt.yaml data. Redline those.
  • E1/E2 keeps P2's D1/D2 exercises but runs its own P3-specific plain table, not P2's numbers.

What it does

Same 6-day pattern-pair cycle as AC1/AC2, restructured for P3: a 1½-rep primer at 80% of B's load (skipped on deload weeks), then a reactive primary + secondary lift with no pause (VBT-metered, same rep scheme on both, load −5% on the secondary), a single VBT-metered accessory movement (D), then an accessory superset (E1/E2) carried over unchanged from P2.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

AC•Axial•P3•5D - Acceleration (AC3 Split · Axial 5D)

When to run this split

  • Acceleration P3, same 5-day reassembly as AC1_AX5/AC2_AX5 - Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V).

Watch for

  • B/C still reactive (no pause), same rep scheme, C reduced ~5% off B - nothing about the day reassembly changes that.

What it does

A 5-day cycle -- Mon Squat/Hinge, Tue Pull(H)/Pull(V), Wed Press(H)/Press(V), Thu off, Sat Press(V)/Pull(V) -- reassembled from the same exercises and numbers as AC3's Axial 6-day cycle (Tue/Wed/Fri reuse D6/D2/D4 unchanged), just fewer days.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

  • Acceleration P3, same 5-day pairing as AC3_AX5, lower-body vehicles swapped non-axial, plus a Friday Primer.

Watch for

  • Friday's Primer is not a lift day - a light plyometric touch into a light reactive touch, well under this phase's real B/C loading.

What it does

Same Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat pattern-pairing as the Axial 5-day, lower-body vehicles swapped non-axial (upper stays machine-based, already non-axial), plus a Friday Primer built from Acceleration's own toolkit (plyometric touch into a light dead-start/paused/reactive touch). Two full recovery days (Thu, plus Friday's own low volume) instead of one.

Period: Base sequence · pre-diagnosis

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

AC•Non-Axial•P3•4D - Acceleration (AC3 Split · Non-Axial 4D)

When to run this split

  • Acceleration P3, volume down significantly for a 4-day week - same Mon/Wed/Sat pattern shape as AC1_NA4/AC2_NA4.

Watch for

  • Pull(H)'s Wednesday slot carries a computed -5% reduction, same as AC1_NA4 (this deficit's Pull(H) is never natively a secondary pattern).
  • Friday's Primer trades the light reactive touch for a slightly faster one - same speed-focused intent as the other two 4-day Primers.

What it does

Volume down significantly: three lift days (Mon Squat/Lunge/Posterior, Wed Hinge/Pull(H)/Press(V) at the heaviest load, Sat Press(H)/Pull(V)/Hinge at higher volume), each a primary + a secondary pattern + a 3rd pattern run as that day's accessory pair (sourced from the 3rd pattern's own accessory vehicles, not the primary's), plus a speed-focused Friday Primer. Two full recovery days (Tue, Thu) instead of one.

Applied Power

LIVE

Power expression over force output. Foundational + expressive, combined.

Combine foundational and expressive patterns for the first time - strength gets expressed athletically, not produced in isolation. VBT Clusters → Complex → French Contrast: reactive cluster-set VBT work, then the same heavy-lift-plus-explosive-partner logic, drawn tighter and faster each phase.

P14 wk
VBT Clusters
Acceleration P3's own reactive, no-pause, VBT-metered lift - delivered as cluster sets so the athlete can hold bar speed at a heavier load than a straight set allows.
80–95%
P24 wk
Complex
A heavy foundational pattern supersetted immediately with a similar, loaded expressive pattern - the PAP window, used on purpose.
82–88%
P34 wk
French Contrast
Heavy foundational → unloaded expressive → light-loaded → overspeed/assisted expressive, for rounds. The peak expression of the deficit.
85–90%

P1 · VBT Clusters (80–95%)

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances.

Who this phase fits

  • An athlete who's been through Force Control and Acceleration, ready to carry that same reactive VBT standard into Applied Power at cluster-set volume.
  • The gentlest introduction to this deficit's logic - no PAP chain yet, just the cluster mechanic itself.

Watch for

  • The intra-set rest between cluster reps is brief (10-15s) - long enough to hold velocity, not a full reset between sets.
  • Move to P2 once the athlete is reliably hitting the velocity zone across every cluster, not just the first one.
AP•Axial•P1•6D - Applied Power (AP1 Split · Axial 6-day)

When to run this split

  • Applied Power P1, always - phase-locked, since P1's week shape (VBT cluster sets, Acceleration P3's own exercises/ladder) only exists on this split. A 6-day cycle, not a literal calendar week.

Watch for

  • The "N+1" set from Acceleration is now a real cluster set here, not an AMRAP finisher - e.g. "5+1 x4" becomes "6x(2x2)clstr" at the same %/velocity target.
  • D (single VBT accessory at C's load) and E1/E2 stay straight sets - only the day's two trained patterns (B/C) are clustered.

What it does

A 6-day pattern-pair cycle (D1 Squat/Lunge, D2 Press(H)/Press(V), D3 Hinge/Pull(V), D4 Lunge/Posterior, D5 Press(V)/Press(H), D6 Pull(H)/Hinge) -- Acceleration P3's exact exercises and VBT ladder, the day's two trained patterns delivered as cluster sets instead of straight-set-plus-AMRAP, a single VBT accessory exposure (D), then an accessory superset (E1/E2).

P2 · Complex (82–88%)

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances.

Who this phase fits

  • An athlete who brings real intent to the expressive partner, ready to feel (and use) the PAP window directly.
  • The heavy set and the explosive set now sit close together on purpose.

Watch for

  • The intracomplex rest (3–4 min) is not optional - cutting it kills the potentiation effect.
  • If time is short, drop a set, don't drop the rest.
AP•Axial•P2•6D - Applied Power (Axial Split 1 · 6-day)

When to run this split

  • Restructure period - throwing load is near zero or just building back up.
  • 6 days, axial vehicles - the ceiling split. Nothing is compromised for throwing yet. Applied Power P2/P3 only - P1 runs on AP1 instead.

Watch for

  • As soon as throwing starts climbing meaningfully, this is the first split to move off of.

What it does

The ceiling. Peak axial load, 6 lift days, every pattern gets a heavy + a light touch. Throwing is trivial, so no consolidation — Wed still carries a lower pattern.

Period: Restructure · low / building

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

AP•Axial•P2•5D - Applied Power (Axial Split 2 · 5-day)

When to run this split

  • Energy period - throwing load is moderate.
  • 5 days, axial vehicles - lifting consolidates onto the two throw-anchor days; lower-body work comes off throw days entirely.

Watch for

  • Still axial (free-bar) - this is the split for moderate throwing demand, not yet high.

What it does

Compresses to 5 days with a Thursday valley. Lifting consolidates onto the Wed & Sat throw anchors (both pure upper); lower comes off throw days. Still axial vehicles.

Period: Energy · moderate

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

AP•Non-Axial•P2•5D - Applied Power (Non-Axial Split 1 · 5-day)

When to run this split

  • Wattage / Integrate period - throwing load is at or near its peak for the cycle.
  • 5 days: Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat match AX2's skeleton with lower-body vehicles de-axialized (leg press, loaded hyper/glute, Jefferson lunge) to shed spinal load exactly when throwing intensity is highest.
  • Friday drops the Lunge/Posterior day for a low-volume, full-body Primer - an overcoming-iso primer supersetted right before a heavy concentric single, lower body then upper.

Watch for

  • The split for in-season peak stretches - move here before a problem shows up, not after.
  • Friday's Primer is not a lift day - two isometric-into-single pairs, not a session to add volume to.

What it does

Same Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat skeleton as Axial 2, lower vehicles de-axialized to shed spinal load as throwing intensity peaks. Friday drops the Lunge/Posterior day for a low-volume, full-body Primer: an overcoming-iso primer supersetted immediately before a heavy concentric single, lower body then upper — a taste of Complex logic at a fraction of the volume.

Period: Wattage / Integrate · high

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

FRI - PRIMER

Not a full lift day — mimics a Complex (isometric primer superset immediately into a heavy concentric single) across the day's key patterns, at a fraction of the volume. Every element is about intent, not accumulation.

Element / ExerciseMethod / Cue Prescription
P1Lower - Overcoming Iso Primer - Overcoming Isometric Squat (bar against pins)Max effort into an immovable pin, no visible bar movement — superset immediately into the heavy single below 2 × 3 s
P2Lower - Heavy Concentric Single - Trap Bar DeadliftMaximal concentric intent off a dead stop, spending the isometric's potentiation immediately 2 × 1 @ 85-90%
P3Upper - Overcoming Iso Primer - Overcoming Isometric Bench Press (bar against pins)Max effort into an immovable pin, no visible bar movement — superset immediately into the heavy single below 2 × 3 s
P4Upper - Heavy Concentric Single - Pause Bench PressMaximal concentric intent off the chest, spending the isometric's potentiation immediately 2 × 1 @ 85-90%

AP•Non-Axial•P2•4D - Applied Power (Non-Axial Split 2 · 4-day)

When to run this split

  • Refine / Engage period - the peak-competition stretch. Applied Power only.
  • Volume down significantly: 3 lift days (Mon/Wed/Sat), each a primary + a slightly-reduced 2nd primary + a 3rd pattern run as that day's accessory (two full supersets, sourced from the 3rd pattern's own accessory vehicles, not the primary's).
  • Two full recovery days (Tue, Thu) plus a Friday Primer - speed-of-movement singles, not heavy load.

Watch for

  • Friday's Primer is not a lift day - a short, low-volume, speed-focused primer, not a fifth training day.
  • The C1a-C2b accessory block on each lift day comes from that day's THIRD pattern, not the primary - check the exercise names, not just the day header, before assuming what's loaded there.

What it does

The peak-competition split — Applied Power only. Volume down significantly: three lift days, each a primary + a slightly-reduced 2nd primary + a 3rd pattern run as that day's accessory superset pair (two total supersets), plus a Friday Primer ahead of the weekend. Two full recovery days (Tue, Thu) instead of one.

Period: Refine / Engage · peak

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

P3 · French Contrast (85–90%)

Testing Day lands every 4th week and decides whether the athlete advances.

Who this phase fits

  • Advanced athletes ready for the full French Contrast chain - four exercises, escalating speed, run for rounds.
  • The peak expression of the deficit - closest the weight room gets to the throwing action itself.

Watch for

  • The most complex, most fatiguing structure in the system - first thing shed when throwing demand spikes.
  • Drop to P2's simpler superset before dropping volume within P3.
AP•Axial•P3•6D - Applied Power (Axial Split 1 · 6-day)

When to run this split

  • Restructure period - throwing load is near zero or just building back up.
  • 6 days, axial vehicles - the ceiling split. Nothing is compromised for throwing yet. Applied Power P2/P3 only - P1 runs on AP1 instead.

Watch for

  • As soon as throwing starts climbing meaningfully, this is the first split to move off of.

What it does

The ceiling. Peak axial load, 6 lift days, every pattern gets a heavy + a light touch. Throwing is trivial, so no consolidation — Wed still carries a lower pattern.

Period: Restructure · low / building

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

AP•Axial•P3•5D - Applied Power (Axial Split 2 · 5-day)

When to run this split

  • Energy period - throwing load is moderate.
  • 5 days, axial vehicles - lifting consolidates onto the two throw-anchor days; lower-body work comes off throw days entirely.

Watch for

  • Still axial (free-bar) - this is the split for moderate throwing demand, not yet high.

What it does

Compresses to 5 days with a Thursday valley. Lifting consolidates onto the Wed & Sat throw anchors (both pure upper); lower comes off throw days. Still axial vehicles.

Period: Energy · moderate

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

AP•Non-Axial•P3•5D - Applied Power (Non-Axial Split 1 · 5-day)

When to run this split

  • Wattage / Integrate period - throwing load is at or near its peak for the cycle.
  • 5 days: Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat match AX2's skeleton with lower-body vehicles de-axialized (leg press, loaded hyper/glute, Jefferson lunge) to shed spinal load exactly when throwing intensity is highest.
  • Friday drops the Lunge/Posterior day for a low-volume, full-body Primer - an overcoming-iso primer supersetted right before a heavy concentric single, lower body then upper.

Watch for

  • The split for in-season peak stretches - move here before a problem shows up, not after.
  • Friday's Primer is not a lift day - two isometric-into-single pairs, not a session to add volume to.

What it does

Same Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat skeleton as Axial 2, lower vehicles de-axialized to shed spinal load as throwing intensity peaks. Friday drops the Lunge/Posterior day for a low-volume, full-body Primer: an overcoming-iso primer supersetted immediately before a heavy concentric single, lower body then upper — a taste of Complex logic at a fraction of the volume.

Period: Wattage / Integrate · high

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

AP•Non-Axial•P3•4D - Applied Power (Non-Axial Split 2 · 4-day)

When to run this split

  • Refine / Engage period - the peak-competition stretch. Applied Power only.
  • Volume down significantly: 3 lift days (Mon/Wed/Sat), each a primary + a slightly-reduced 2nd primary + a 3rd pattern run as that day's accessory (two full supersets, sourced from the 3rd pattern's own accessory vehicles, not the primary's).
  • Two full recovery days (Tue, Thu) plus a Friday Primer - speed-of-movement singles, not heavy load.

Watch for

  • Friday's Primer is not a lift day - a short, low-volume, speed-focused primer, not a fifth training day.
  • The C1a-C2b accessory block on each lift day comes from that day's THIRD pattern, not the primary - check the exercise names, not just the day header, before assuming what's loaded there.

What it does

The peak-competition split — Applied Power only. Volume down significantly: three lift days, each a primary + a slightly-reduced 2nd primary + a 3rd pattern run as that day's accessory superset pair (two total supersets), plus a Friday Primer ahead of the weekend. Two full recovery days (Tue, Thu) instead of one.

Period: Refine / Engage · peak

2-week

2-week peak fortnight: load ramps to the top of the band; re-diagnosis at the end of W2 (no separate deload).

How to Adjust

This is the judgment layer: how a coach actually moves an athlete through these programs over time. (For editing the underlying data files themselves - loads, exercises, splits - see the Technical Note at the bottom; that's a separate, much rarer task.)

Progressing or regressing a phase

Phases move on a re-diagnosis tick, not a fixed calendar: at the end of every block (W2 for a 2-week block, W4 for 4-week, W4 and W8 for 8-week), re-assess the athlete - typically a force-plate touch plus how the block actually went - and decide to hold, advance, or regress.

Advance when the athlete has met the current phase's "watch for" bar (see the per-deficit, per-phase notes above) across the full load band - not just on a good day.

Regress without hesitation after a layoff, an injury, or a block where the held stop broke down - dropping back a phase is a normal, expected tool, not a failure.

Switching splits as throwing demand changes

The split should track the athlete's throwing calendar, not their lifting progress. Move Restructure → Energy → Wattage/Integrate → Refine/Engage as throwing climbs; move back down as the throwing period resets.

A phase change and a split change are independent decisions - it's normal for an athlete to stay in the same phase for a full season while their split changes multiple times underneath it. Movement Literacy is the one exception: its splits (ML1/ML2/ML3) are phase-locked, not throwing-demand-governed, because the week's actual SHAPE changes with the phase there - a phase change on Movement Literacy IS a split change.

Choosing a duration

Default to 4 weeks - it's the block length everything else (re-diagnosis cadence, deload placement) is built around.

Use 2 weeks for a short runway, or as a deliberately abbreviated re-acclimation touch - e.g. bringing an advanced athlete back into a phase for a quick, real check before moving them up.

Use 8 weeks for a long runway or when the goal is deep consolidation of the quality rather than a quick re-diagnosis - it's two 4-week ticks back to back, with the second adding volume, not load.

The re-diagnosis cadence

Every block ends in a deload + re-diagnosis week (marked ▽ in the programs), except the 2-week block, which is a peak fortnight with no separate deload - the re-diagnosis happens right at the load peak.

Treat the re-diagnosis point as the only place decisions about phase/split/duration should change. Making that call mid-block trades away the one thing a block is supposed to give you: a clean before/after read on the athlete.

Technical note

Day-to-day programming changes (a load %, a set/rep scheme, an exercise swap, a new split) don't need any of this site touched - they're edited directly in this project's data/ files (waves.yaml, exercises.yaml, phases.yaml, splits.yaml) and both this site and the .xlsx rebuild from the same source. See the project README for the exact file-by-file guide.

VeloU Strength - generated from data, not hand-written.
